335271.title: The odd-order edge lower-bound conjecture for k-in-out graphs
335271.literal_statement:
A **$k$-in-out graph** is a directed graph satisfying the single visit and paired vertices conditions, with parameter $k$. For odd $k$, consider such graphs of order $2k+1$.

**Odd-order edge lower-bound conjecture.** Any $k$-in-out graph of order $2k+1$ for odd $k$ has at least $4k-3$ edges.

The construction discussed in the source has $4k-3$ edges for odd $k$, while the general lower bound known there is only $4k-4$. No examples with $4k-4$ edges were known for odd $k$, motivating this conjecture.

The intended statement fails trivially at k=1 (one vertex, 0 = 4k-4 arcs), a zero-credit smallest-case defect. The substantive question is odd k >= 5 (no 3-in-out graph has order 5, per the source).
mechanism_and_coverage: Normal form (from the source's own proof of Thm. edges): a k-in-out graph of order 2k-1 with exactly 4k-4 arcs has every arc on some paired Hamiltonian path, its vertices split into I, O, B, N with |N|=|B|-1, and every vertex of X = I u N has out-degree exactly 2 (heads in I u B) and every vertex of Y = O u N has in-degree exactly 2 (tails in O u B). In this form the single visit condition holds automatically (each incoming->outgoing path has one more B-vertex than N-vertex).

Exhaustive search over this normal form, labelling the vertices along one Hamiltonian path i_1 -> o_1 (scripts/kinout.py): k=3: 33 graphs, 0 solutions (matches the source); k=4: 5005 graphs, 12 solutions (control); k=5: all a=0..4, 70 type words, 1,595,041 graphs, 0 solutions. Independent backtracking re-check of k=5 (scripts/kinout_bt.py): 0 solutions. k=6, a=0, first-option chunk 0: 18 solutions (control).

New structural lemma (proved in SUMMARY.md): in any such solution the out-pairs of X form a spanning tree T_out on I u B and the in-pairs of Y form a spanning tree T_in on O u B; hence between any start and any end there is at most one Hamiltonian path, and the closed successor permutation satisfies f_{s',t} = (s s') f_{s,t} and f_{s,t'} = f_{s,t} (t t') for tree-adjacent s,s' and t,t'. Every found even-k solution (k=4, a in {0,1}; k=6, a=0) has both trees equal to Hamiltonian paths (scripts/kinout_treedeg.py).
Path-tree model (a=0): F_{S,T} = tau B_S^{-1} mu B_T with B_T = (1 2 ... T); exhaustive over all (tau, mu): k=4: 4 solutions, k=5: 0, k=6: 24, k=7: 0 (3,628,800 pairs) (scripts/kinout_perm.py).
335271.remaining_lemmas: L1: in every 4k-4-arc solution both trees are paths (empirical only). L2: the path-tree model has no solution for odd k (verified k=5,7, a=0 only; the a>=1 analogue is not yet derived). A proof of L1+L2 for all odd k would settle the intended conjecture; the Lean cost would be high (Hamiltonian paths for general k).

335352.title: Permutation conjecture for a rational function on roots of unity
335352.literal_statement:
Let $k$ be an even integer and set $q=5^k$. Let

$$
\mu_{q+1}=\{x\in {\mathbb F}_{q^2}:x^{q+1}=1\}
$$

be the group of $(q+1)$-st roots of unity in ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$. **Permutation conjecture.** The rational function

$$
-x\left(\frac{x^2-2}{x^2+2}\right)^2
$$

permutes $\mu_{q+1}$.
If true, this would yield a class of permutation trinomials over finite fields through the relation between permutation polynomials over ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$ and rational functions on $\mu_{q+1}$ described in the surrounding argument.

335382.title: Existence of angle labelings for essentially 3-connected maps
335382.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a map on a genus $g\geq 1$ orientable surface. An **edge, positive-vertex, positive-face angle labeling** means a labeling with the edge condition and positive vertex and face conditions indicated by those parameters. A map is **essentially 3-connected** when its universal-cover graph is 3-connected in the relevant essential sense. **The angle-labeling conjecture.** $G$ admits an edge, $\mathbb{N}^*$-vertex, $\mathbb{N}^*$-face angle labeling if and only if it is essentially 3-connected.

The “only if” direction is supported by the cited proposition and lemma; the converse is proposed as the general-map analogue of the preceding triangulation conjecture.

335553.title: The regularity conjecture for the $k$-abelian complexity of automatic sequences
335553.literal_statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and let $\omega$ be an $\ell$-automatic sequence, meaning that its $\ell$-kernel is finite. The $k$-abelian complexity of $\omega$ is the sequence counting the $k$-abelian equivalence classes of factors of each length.

**Automatic-sequence regularity conjecture.** The $k$-abelian complexity of any $\ell$-automatic sequence is an $\ell$-regular sequence.

The conjecture generalizes the previously conjectured—and independently proved—case of the $2$-abelian complexity of the Thue–Morse sequence. The paper presents the $3$-regularity of the $k$-abelian complexity of the Cantor sequence as supporting evidence; the general assertion remains open in the supplied source.

335721.title: Deletion conjecture for unavoidable formulas with reversal
335721.literal_statement:
Let $phi$ be a formula with reversal, and let $X$ be its set of two-way variables. Write $delta_{X\cup X^R}(phi)$ for the formula obtained by deleting all occurrences of the two-way variables in $X$ and their reversals $X^R$.

**Deletion conjecture.** If $phi$ is unavoidable, then $delta_{X\cup X^R}(phi)$ is unavoidable.

This conjecture is proposed as a possible route toward the generalized Zimin divisibility conjecture. The paper notes that the analogous factor property for one-way variables does not generalize directly when there are at least three one-way variables, while the preservation of unavoidability after deleting two-way variables remains plausible and open.

335976.title: Fraenkel's conjecture on complementary Beatty sequences
335976.literal_statement:
Let $d\geq 3$, let $\alpha_1<\alpha_2<\ldots<\alpha_d$, and let $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_d$ be real numbers. Suppose that the vectors

$$
(\lfloor n\alpha_i+\gamma_i\rfloor)_{i=1}^d,
$$

for $n\in\mathbb{N}$, split the positive integers. **Fraenkel's conjecture.** Then

$$
\alpha_i=\frac{2^d-1}{2^{d-i}},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d.
$$

This is the nonhomogeneous rational-modulus form of Fraenkel's conjecture on partitions of the positive integers by Beatty-type sequences. The statement concerns the uniqueness of the moduli, while the shifts $\gamma_i$ are unrestricted; the source presents it as a conjecture and gives historical references to work on special cases.

336226.title: Zvonkine's topological-recursion conjecture for orbifold $r$-spin Hurwitz numbers
336226.literal_statement:
Let $g\geq 0$ and $n\geq 1$. For positive integers $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n$, let $h_{g;\mu}^{\circ,q,r}$ be the connected $q$-orbifold $r$-spin Hurwitz number, and define the formal symmetric $n$-differential

$$
W_{g,n}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=d_1\otimes\cdots\otimes d_n\sum_{\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n=1}^{\infty}h_{g;\mu}^{\circ,q,r}\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\mu_i}.
$$

Let $\omega_{g,n}(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be symmetric $n$-differentials on the spectral curve with parametrization $x(z)=ze^{-z^{qr}}$ and $y(z)=z^q$. **Zvonkine's topological-recursion conjecture.** The formal differentials $W_{g,n}$ are expansions in $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of the differentials $\omega_{g,n}$, and the latter satisfy topological recursion on this spectral curve.

336454.title: The Colin de Verdière graph complement conjecture
336454.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement. Let $\mu(G)$ denote the Colin de Verdière parameter. **Colin de Verdière's graph complement conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\mu(G)+\mu(\overline{G})\geq |V(G)|-2.
$$

336558.literal_statement:

$$
C(N,q,\{1,\ldots,1\})=o\left(q^{\left\lceil\frac{N}{t-1}\right\rceil}\right).

336620.title: Mubayi–Stein threshold conjecture for tight-path Ramsey parameters
336620.literal_statement:
For integers $3\leq t\leq k$, let $\overline r_k(k+1,t;P_n)$ be the least $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the $k$-sets of an $N$-vertex set contains a blue tight path $P_n$ or has a $(k+1)$-vertex set inducing at least $t$ red edges. Define $\operatorname{twr}_1(x)=x$ and $\operatorname{twr}_{i+1}(x)=2^{\operatorname{twr}_i(x)}$. **Mubayi–Stein conjecture.** There are positive constants $c=c(k,t)$ and $c'=c'(k,t)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{twr}_{t-2}(n^c)<\overline r_k(k+1,t;P_n)<\operatorname{twr}_{t-2}(n^{c'}).
$$

This is the tight-path analogue of the Erdős–Hajnal tower-growth conjecture for cliques. The source presents it as open.

336718.finding: The source gives M_{2n}(complement I_v,q) = q^{2n(n-1)} P_n(q), P_n = sum_i (-1)^i C(n,i)[2n-i]!_q. The count depends only on the number n of forbidden cells in distinct rows and columns. A completion argument reduces it to full-rank n x 2n matrices with n forced zeros: P_n = [n]!_q Q_n(2n), where Q_j(m) = sum_i (-1)^i C(j,i)[m-i]_q...[m-j+1]_q (a q-count of fixed-point-free injections [j]->[m]). Computed: P_n in N[q] for n<=30. For 3<=j<=13 and j<=m<=j+12, Q_j(m) is in N[q] exactly when m >= 2j-1; for j=1,2 it is in N[q] for every m>=j; j=14 is negative for all m<=26 (scripts/qdiag.py 30). This threshold is a new observation from computation, not a theorem. Tried and failed: Q_j(m) = q[m-1]Q_{j-1}(m-1)+...; F(m,j) = [m]F(m-1,j)+...; Q_j(m) = q^a Q_j(m-1)+B Q_{j-1}(m-1) (works for j<=2 only).

336736.title: The feasibility interval for the undirected optical-index ratio
336736.literal_statement:
Let $\delta\geq 1$ be a rational number. Call $\delta$ **feasible** if there exists a simple graph $G$ such that

$$
\frac{w(G)}{\pi(G)}=\delta.
$$

**The feasibility-interval conjecture.** Any rational number $\delta$ satisfying

$$
1\leq\delta\leq\frac{3}{2}
$$

is feasible.
The paper establishes feasibility for several infinite families of values, including values arising from complete $m$-ary trees. Whether every rational number in the interval is feasible remains open.

336742.title: The four-list conjecture for facial unique-maximum edge-coloring
336742.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph. A **FUM-edge-coloring** is a facial edge-coloring in which every face is incident with a unique edge colored with the maximal color appearing on that face. Suppose each edge $e$ is assigned a list $L(e)$ of four integers.

**Four-list conjecture.** If each edge of a plane graph is assigned a list of $4$ integers, then there exists a FUM-edge-coloring assigning each edge a color from its list.

This is the list-coloring analogue of the proposed four-color bound for FUM-edge-coloring. The source presents it as an expectation and gives no resolution, so it remains open.

336747.title: Polynomial domination conjecture for directed-triangle-free digraphs
336747.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a digraph. A digraph is **directed-triangle-free** if it contains no directed cycle of length three, $\alpha(G)$ denotes its independence number, and $\gamma(G)$ denotes its domination number.

**Polynomial domination conjecture.** There is an integer $\ell$ such that if $G$ is a directed-triangle-free digraph with $\alpha(D)=\alpha$, then

$$
\gamma(G)\leq\alpha^{\ell}.
$$

This is the domination-number consequence of the conjecture that the dichromatic number of a directed-triangle-free digraph is bounded by a polynomial in its independence number. The source presents it as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.
